scenes.heading: Planning your student investigation
scenes.say: In Unit 1, you design and run your own investigation. A good plan gives results you can trust. And these skills turn up again and again in VCE exams.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A fair 100 m race: same track, same start, only the runner differs
scenes.science: A fair test: change only the IV, measure the DV, control the rest
scenes.breaks: In a race you just pick a winner. In an investigation you test 4–5 IV values and look for a trend.
scenes.say: Think of a fair hundred metre race. Everyone runs the same distance, on the same track, with the same start. Only the runner changes. In an investigation, that's your independent variable. The time on the clock is your dependent variable. But instead of picking a winner, you test four or five values and look for a trend.
scenes.caption: Think of a fair 100 m race. Everyone runs the same distance, on the same track, with the same start. Only the runner changes. In an investigation, that's your independent variable. The time on the clock is your dependent variable. But instead of picking a winner, you test 4 or 5 values and look for a trend.

scenes.heading: Variables and controls
points: IV: the one thing you change (x-axis)
Control: the baseline group for comparison
scenes.say: You change the independent variable. The dependent variable depends on it. Controlled variables stay the same in every trial. And don't mix those up with a control, which is the baseline group you compare against, like a resting, zero minute condition.

scenes.heading: Plan it step by step
steps: Check ethics and do a risk assessment
scenes.say: Start with a focused, testable question. Write a hypothesis: if, then, because. Write a method someone else could repeat, with replicates and safety steps. Check ethics, like informed consent. Then graph the means, describe the trend, and explain it with biology. Results support a hypothesis. They never prove it.

scenes.heading: Random vs systematic error

left.title: Random error
points: Fix: more replicates, take the mean

right.title: Systematic error
points: All results off in the same direction

scenes.say: Random error makes results scatter, like a scale that reads slightly differently each time. Take more replicates and average them. Systematic error pushes every result the same way, like a scale that's always two kilos heavy. Repeating won't help. Random equals repeat, systematic equals swap.

scenes.heading: Spot the outlier
scenes.question: Heart rate after 2 minutes of stepping, three trials: 112, 115 and 148 beats per minute. What is the mean?
lines: 148 is far from the others: an outlier
scenes.say: Three trials give one hundred and twelve, one hundred and fifteen, and one hundred and forty-eight beats per minute. One hundred and forty-eight is an outlier. Maybe the participant didn't rest long enough. Leave it out, and say so. The mean of the other two is about one hundred and fourteen beats per minute.
scenes.caption: Three trials give 112, 115 and 148 beats per minute. 148 is an outlier. Maybe the participant didn't rest long enough. Leave it out, and say so. The mean of the other two is about 114 beats per minute.

points: Change one IV, measure one DV
scenes.say: Quick recap. Change one independent variable and measure one dependent variable. Your hypothesis needs a because. Use replicates and a control. And remember: random equals repeat, systematic equals swap. Now try the practice questions!
